## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical policy design for multi-tenant security with Kyverno/OPA, covering image provenance, secret handling, pod security, networking, and runtime controls.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper policies
- Image digest pinning and registry whitelisting
- SecretStore/secretRef guidance
- Pod security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem
- NetworkPolicy default-deny with tenant exceptions
- Ephemeral containers and privileged checks

## Code Example
```yaml
# sample Kyverno policy excerpt
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: deny-privileged-host
spec:
  rules:
  - excludes:
      any:
        - context: {}
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: "Privileged and host namespace usage is disallowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - SecurityContext:
                  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test these policies across multi-cloud clusters?
- What would you monitor to detect bypass attempts or misconfigurations?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime security controls that span CI, policy engines, and multi cloud networking, ensuring outbound traffic is strictly controlled and auditable.

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (Gatekeeper/OPA)
- Egress gateway design and TLS origination
- Outbound allowlist management
- CI validation for policy enforcement
- Cross-cloud consistency and testing

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate for Gatekeeper enforcing egress gateway annotation
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8segressgateway
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sEgressPolicy
  targets:
  - target: obj  # pseudo example for clarity
    rego: |
      package k8segress
      default deny = true
      deny[msg] = msg {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["egress.gateway/enforced"] == "true"
        msg := "Pod must set egress.gateway/enforced=true to route via central gateway"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint demonstrating allowlist usage (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sEgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-egress-gateway
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
  parameters:
    allowlist: ["app.allowed.example.com"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no egress annotation or disallowed destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-egress-pod
  annotations:
    # missing or false
    egress.gateway/enforced: "false"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (annotation set and allowlisted destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-egress-pod
  annotations:
    egress.gateway/enforced: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23.4
```

- Local: run gatekeeper locally to test ConstraintTemplate/Constraint; simulate Pod admission with k8s manifest.
- CI: run a workflow that lints manifests, validates policy via a test cluster or KinD, and fails on noncompliant manifests.

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-as-code skills for multi-tenant Kubernetes environments
- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

Failing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: insecure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "64Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "128Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
```

CI Validation Steps
```bash
# Install Kyverno CLI
brew install kyverno

# Validate policies against manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest deployment.yaml

# CI/CD integration example (GitHub Actions)
- name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
  run: |
    kyverno apply policy.yaml -f deploy/
```

Runtime Gate Demonstration
```bash
# Apply the policy cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Verify policy is active
kubectl get clusterpolicy require-secure-deployments

# Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest (will fail)
kubectl apply -f insecure-deployment.yaml
# Error: Validation failed: Each container must define a secure securityContext...

# Deploy compliant manifest (will succeed)
kubectl apply -f secure-deployment.yaml
# deployment.apps/secure-app created
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

- YAML manifest parsing

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions snippet (validation)
name: Validate Provenance
on: [push]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Inspect image for digest and labels
        run: |
          CONTAINER_IMG='registry.example.com/feature-service@sha256:abcdef...'
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' $CONTAINER_IMG | cut -d'@' -f2)
          LABELS=$(docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Labels}}' $CONTAINER_IMG)
          if [[ -z "$DIGEST" || "$LABELS" != *data_version* || "$LABELS" != *model_version* ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Canary trace test
        run: |
          # pseudo-step: send request and verify OTLP trace propagates
          curl -sS http://feature-service.canary/health -H 'traceparent: 00-abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789-1234567812345678-01' >/dev/null
          # verification would query OTLP collector for trace-id
          echo 'Canary test passed'
```

 rules:

## Why This Is Asked

In production Kubernetes environments, ensuring supply-chain security for Helm-based deployments is critical. This question evaluates your ability to integrate multiple security tools—Helm templating, SBOM generation, and image signature verification—into a cohesive CI gate. It tests practical knowledge of enforcing provenance and attestations before code merges.

## Key Concepts

- **Helm templating and values extraction**: Rendering charts to discover all container images referenced in deployments
- **SBOM generation**: Using Syft to create a CycloneDX SBOM that catalogs all dependencies and artifacts
- **Image signing verification**: Using cosign to validate container image signatures against a public key stored in the repository
- **CI gate integration**: Implementing fail-fast behavior in GitHub Actions to block unsigned images and missing attestations

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for Helm image signing enforcement
name: Helm Image Security Gate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  helm-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Install Helm and Syft
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh

      - name: Render Helm templates
        run: helm template my-app ./chart --values values.yaml --output-dir ./rendered

      - name: Extract image references
        run: |
          grep -rh 'image:' ./rendered | awk '{print $2}' > images.txt

      - name: Generate SBOM with Syft
        run: |
          syft $(cat images.txt) -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Verify image signatures with cosign
        run: |
          COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY=cosign.pub
          for IMAGE in $(cat images.txt); do
            cosign verify --key $COSIGN_PUBLIC_KEY $IMAGE || exit 1
          done
```

## Code Example

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in k8s/**/*.yaml; do
  if grep -E \"apiVersion:\s*(extensions/v1beta1|apps/v1beta1|networking.k8s.io/v1beta1)\" \"$f\" >/dev/null; then
    echo \"Deprecated apiVersion found in $f\"

  fi
done
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical data validation in CI/CD with a concrete schema and gating.

## Key Concepts
- CSV header validation
- Type coercion and data quality
- CI gate integration (GitHub Actions)

## Code Example
```python
import csv, sys
from datetime import datetime

EXPECTED = {
  'id': int,
  'date': 'date',
  'amount': float,
  'category': str
}

DATE_FMT = '%Y-%m-%d'

def parse_row(row):
  row['id'] = int(row['id'])
  row['date'] = datetime.strptime(row['date'], DATE_FMT).date()
  row['amount'] = float(row['amount'])
  row['category'] = str(row['category'])
  return row

def main(path):
  with open(path, newline='') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    header = set(reader.fieldnames or [])
    if header != set(EXPECTED.keys()):
      print('Header mismatch:', reader.fieldnames)
      sys.exit(1)
    for r in reader:
      try:
        parse_row(r)
      except Exception as e:
        print('Type/Parse error', e, r)
        sys.exit(1)
  print('OK')

if __name__ == '__main__':
  sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1]))
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for evolving schemas without breaking the pipeline?
- How would you test locally with representative failing/passing CSVs?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic understanding of Kubernetes security posture and practical gate design in CI, covering both Pod security and NetworkPolicy defaults.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext and container.securityContext
- Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper for policy enforcement
- Default-deny NetworkPolicy per Namespace
- Local validation with kubectl and kyverno/opa tooling
- CI validation with GitHub Actions hooks

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and runAsNonRoot: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              runAsNonRoot: true
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# NetworkPolicy default-deny (Namespace scope)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the policy to exclude specific namespaces or namespaces with legacy workloads?
- How would you test this in a multi-tenant CI environment with limited cluster access?
